title: observability-weekly-2026-04-27
content:
Observability team - weekly notes (2026-04-27)
Owner: Marcus Chen
Summary:
- Focus this week: tracing ingestion reliability, dashboard refresh for Dedicated capacity telemetry, and cost-telemetry spike investigation on April 24th.
- Outcome highlights: rolled back an ingestion config change that reduced trace drop-rate from ~8% to ~1.5%; new dashboard widgets merged for per-model cost breakdown; initial RCA drafted for spike and follow-up actions scheduled.

Standup highlights (daily):
- Mon 04/20: Tracing ingestion regression observed after agent upgrade; started hotfix investigation.
- Tue 04/21: Hotfix deployed to canary, metrics looked stable on canary; plan to roll to prod in low-traffic window.
- Wed 04/22: Prod rollout started at 02:00 UTC, observed immediate reduction in trace drops; continued monitoring.
- Thu 04/23: Began work on dashboards for Dedicated capacity cost attribution (per-customer / per-model).
- Fri 04/24: Cost telemetry spike (GPU billing) observed — investigating correlation with batch sizes and autoscaler behavior.

Meetings and notes:
- Weekly sync (Tue 04/21):
  - Attendees: Marcus, Elena, Sofia, Tom, Priya (SRE).
  - Agenda:
    1) Tracing ingestion post-upgrade regression
    2) Dashboard backlog prioritization
    3) Cost telemetry anomaly update
  - Decisions:
    - Revert agent change that introduced a race in span batching (PR linked).
    - Prioritize Dedicated cost breakdown dashboard before next customer review (deadline 2026-05-05).
    - Create a cost-alert rule for >20% day-over-day GPU billing increase per cluster.

- Tracing deep-dive (Thu 04/23):
  - Root cause: upstream agent changed buffer flush semantics which led to intermittent span loss under high concurrency.
  - Evidence: spike in span_none counter and increased sampler drop events on hosts with >500 concurrent inferences.
  - Fix implemented: rollback flush change + added stricter unit/integration tests simulating high concurrency.
  - Follow-ups:
    - Add synthetic load test to CI (owner: Tom, ETA: 2026-05-04).
    - Add trace drop-rate alert to PagerDuty rotation (owner: Elena, ETA: 2026-04-30).

Dashboards and observability surface:
- Completed: per-model token-rate and p50/p95 latency widgets for Dedicated telemetry (merged PR: linked).
- In progress: cost attribution panel (per-customer, per-model, per-route) using billing export join (Sofia). Expected to be previewable by 2026-04-30.
- Tech notes:
  - Billing export join runs nightly and surfaces cost by allocation_key. Missing allocation_key on some jobs caused mismatch; created migration to backfill (db-mig-obs-2026-04).
  - Dashboard perf: replaced a heavy nested subquery with pre-aggregated materialized view which reduced load time from ~12s to ~1.4s for the cost dashboard.

Cost telemetry spike (04/24) - initial RCA:
- Symptom: GPU billing increased ~34% for cluster-us-west-2 for the 24-hour window starting 04/24 00:00 UTC.
- Investigation steps:
  - Correlated autoscaler logs with job traces; noticed a set of large-batch jobs (batch-size=64) submitted by experimental workload group.
  - Found autoscaler policy mis-evaluated headroom due to stale metrics (1m aggregation instead of 10s), causing over-provisioning for 30m spikes.
- Mitigation taken:
  - Temporarily tightened autoscaler thresholds for the experiment namespace (Tom).
  - Added alert for sustained >15% variance in allocation vs. historical baseline (Elena).
- Next actions:
  - Change autoscaler metric aggregation window to 10s for inference pools (owner: Infra team, coord: Marcus, ETA: 2026-05-03).
  - Build per-route cost guardrail for experimental jobs to limit burst to 2x baseline (owner: Sofia, ETA: 2026-05-07).

Action items (tracked):
- Tom: Add synthetic high-concurrency trace load test to CI; create test data and runner. (ETA 2026-05-04)
- Elena: Add PagerDuty alert for trace drop-rate >1% (ETA 2026-04-30)
- Sofia: Finish cost-attribution panel and backfill allocation_key; coordinate with billing team for validation. (ETA 2026-04-30 preview, 2026-05-05 final)
- Marcus: Coordinate autoscaler aggregation change with Infra and ensure rollout plan includes canary testing. (ETA 2026-05-03)
- Priya (SRE): Run post-mortem checklist for the trace regression and publish to Confluence (ETA 2026-04-29).

Blockers:
- Waiting on billing team approval for backfill migration window (Sofia).
- Infra capacity for running CI synthetic load tests concurrently with nightly e2e; need to schedule (Tom/Infra).

Risks / Notes:
- If autoscaler aggregation change is applied without canary, we risk oscillations with very spiky traffic; canary plan required.
- Experimental workloads continue to be the largest driver of short-term cost variance — need long-term quota/guardrails.

Metrics snapshot (as of 2026-04-27 08:00 UTC):
- Trace drop-rate (7d avg): 1.6% (target <1%).
- Traces ingested/day: 12.1M
- Cost/day (GPU): $28.3k (7d avg: $22.8k)
- Dashboard load p95: 1.4s

Notes to self / running TODOs:
- Prepare slides for infra review on 2026-05-06: include cost spike RCA and proposed guardrails.
- Follow up with Product on Dedicated cost dashboard requirements for upcoming customer review (Marcus).

References and links:
- Tracing rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/214
- Confluence post-mortem template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Postmortem+Template
- Billing export schema: internal:/billing/export/schema/latest

End of weekly notes.
